answer: Practically, the chain should pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because yarrow only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, jade is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any oasis approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
